disposition_reason: Table 1 and 2 print PXRF means of K, Ca, Mn, Fe, Zn, Rb and Sr in turmeric and curry powders by origin and branding; arsenic and lead are only stated qualitatively as below 1 mg/kg.

study.design: market survey of turmeric and curry powder for mineral provision
study.origin: East Africa (Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda); growing origin not stated
study.market: market establishments in Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda, procured during a project workshop and refugee camp visits
study.method: portable XRF (HD Mobile, monochromatic excitation), powders in sample cups, 3 x 30 s readings, manufacturer calibration
study.lod_text: LODs 3.9 mg/kg (Rb) to 1040 mg/kg (K); LOQs 13 mg/kg (Rb) to 3480 mg/kg (K); As and Pb limits not stated

controls.outcome: K, Fe and Rb significantly higher in branded; Ca, Mn, Zn, Sr not different (Table 2); As and Pb below 1 mg/kg in all samples (data not shown)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: WHO maximum tolerable lead concentration in spices as cited

unresolved: Arsenic and lead are stated only as 'less than 1 mg kg-1 (Data not shown)' for all turmeric and curry samples (p. 6); no numeric findings recorded. PXRF detection limits for As and Pb are not given, so the statement cannot be checked against an LOD.
Per-sample results are in Supplementary Table S1, which is not with the PDF.
Number of samples per spice and per origin within the 40 samples is not stated in the main text.
Daily intake estimates (Table 3) are derived values, not concentrations.
